handledWell: The way Filipinos actually write pesos survives intact. "1,500.00", "PHP25,000", "25000.00 PHP", "25 000" and a value pasted out of Excel with a trailing tab all reach the row as the right number — the browser's number input discards the separators and the currency word before React ever sees them. The feared outcome (a comma truncating 1,500 to 1) does not happen anywhere I tested.

HTML is escaped, not rendered. A tag and an stored in an e-voucher note and a customer note came back as literal text in the list, the detail panel and the voucher panel — zero elements, the handler never fired. React's default escaping holds where send-feedback-email's raw interpolation (N3) does not. (One caveat: RichTextDisplay in QuotationBuilderV3 renders quotation Scope of Services and Terms & Conditions through dangerouslySetInnerHTML with no sanitizer — MemoPanel uses DOMPurify and MessageBubble sanitizes, that one does not. Not reachable by a careless user typing, since tiptap escapes what you type, so not counted as a finding here.)

Emoji, Chinese and right-to-left Arabic round-trip byte-for-byte and do not wreck layout — the customer detail page with an Arabic phrase mid-sentence had scrollWidth exactly equal to innerWidth, no horizontal scroll, no column blow-out.
A 10,000-character note is stored whole (10,095 chars in, 10,095 out) and rendered without truncating or crashing the detail page.

The date fields that matter most are calendar-only, so the classic bad-date strings cannot be typed into them at all: the e-voucher Payment Due Date and the booking ETD / ETA / cut-off fields are custom pickers rendered as buttons, not text inputs. "31/02/2026", "2026-13-45" and "N/A" have nowhere to go.
Leading zeros are handled correctly on the common path — "00042" lands as 42 in every amount field tested.

The vendor and catalog pickers held the line: no free text reached a line item anywhere. Vendor is registry-only, the expense line demanded a real catalog category and item, and the billing line demanded a Billing Catalog item — the catalog doctrine survives careless typing even though it is only a form convention at the API (G5).

Every write that reported success and that I could check WAS in the database. Nothing in this pass produced a LIES_SAYS_SAVED of the N6 kind — the failures here are wrong values honestly saved, not saves that never happened.

Whether the 0.0x collapse also reaches the QUOTATION line-item forms. AddLineItemModal, BrokerageFormV2, MarineInsuranceFormV2 and FinancialSummaryPanel all carry a placeholder="0.00" number input; I only read them, I did not drive them.

Real clipboard paste (Ctrl+V from the OS clipboard) as distinct from keyboard insertText. Chrome's number input sanitises both the same way in my probes, but I could not get a genuine OS-level paste through the harness to be certain.

notes:
The centre of gravity of this pass is a single line, repeated across every money form in the product:

    onChange={e => onChange(parseFloat(e.target.value) || 0)}

on an <input type="number">. It looks defensive. It is the opposite. Chrome reports an intermediate invalid value — "0.0", "-", "1e" — as the empty string; parseFloat("") is NaN; `|| 0` turns that into 0; and React writes the 0 back into the controlled field, destroying the characters already typed. The digits the user types next land in a field that no longer says what they think it says. Nothing errors. Nothing is red. The number is just wrong, and it is wrong by a factor of 100 or 1000 or by its sign.

Two variants, and they fail differently:
  value={x || ""}      (e-voucher, collections) — the field BLANKS, so 0.05 → 5
  value={x}            (billing price)          — the field STICKS at 0 and can
                                                  never be cleared, so -500 → 500

That is why "type it, don't paste it" is load-bearing in the spec, and why every probe uses page.keyboard.type with a delay. Pasting the same strings whole misses the bug completely — the value arrives in one event, parseFloat sees a valid number, and everything looks fine. Any future harness that fills these fields with .fill() will report a clean sweep over a broken product. That is the K1 shape again, in a new place.

The second thing worth saying: the scariest input in this system is not a comma. It is a decimal point after a zero, and a minus sign. Both are things a real accounting person types every week — centavo-level VASP and processing fees are already in this dataset at ₱10, ₱50, ₱61.60, and a credit line on a billing tab is ordinary work. Neither is an attack. Neither produces a complaint.

Third: the two findings that compound with what is already on the register. The .exe upload is M1 with a weapon in it — the bucket was already known to be world-readable, but nobody had put an executable in it and fetched it back anonymously. And the padded customer name is not a curiosity: dev already has 13 untrimmed names cloned verbatim from prod, so the duplicate-master problem is not hypothetical, it is live, and the form that creates it neither trims nor warns.

On honesty: three things I could have written up and did not. The long-filename upload failure is intermittent (2 of 4 runs) and is recorded as such in the spec rather than asserted. The collection panel's DB landing is unproven and is listed as unmeasured, not as a finding. And the ETD/ETA claim has no validation in the code but was never forced through the UI, so it stays in the unmeasured list. A probe that lies is worse than no probe.

The spec is five tests, ~2.6 minutes, all green, and its assertions are phrased so that they fail when the bugs are FIXED as well as if the bugs get worse — each one carries a message saying which. It is a characterisation harness for the current behaviour, not a wall of red. Everything it creates carries E2E-MISUSE and is removed in afterAll including the storage object, and I verified zero leftovers by service-role census after the final run. A second agent was writing E2E-MISUSE-tagged vouchers to dev at the same time; I identified my own rows by actor and content and left theirs alone.

Screenshots: docs/qa/misuse/ (P1 the 0.05→5 field, P2 the sign flip, P4 the year-52026 invoice with a 2020 due date, P5 the two identical customers, P6 the accepted .exe, plus the raw-HTML/RTL note and the 10k-character note pages).

handledWell: A client-rejected quotation is genuinely terminal, and it is guarded by ABSENCE OF AFFORDANCE rather than by a validation message — the only kind of guard a hurried person cannot argue with. notes:
HOW TO READ THIS PASS. Every verdict below came from typing in the UI and then reading the row back with the service-role key (K1) — no toast, no HTTP 200 and no 'no error' was taken as evidence. The spec prints, for each step, what was typed and what landed, side by side. Verdicts are graded STOPPED / WARNED / WROTE_IT_DOWN / BLOCKED_WRONGLY, and WROTE_IT_DOWN — the system cheerfully accepting nonsense — is the finding, not the error.

THE SPEC RUNS GREEN: 4 tests, all passing, verified on two consecutive full runs (~2.1 min). One intermediate run had a single flake in the booking-expenses test (the same test passes in isolation in 46s); the dev server was shared with at least one other agent writing E2E-MISUSE fixtures at the time, which is the E5/E16 slowness already on record. Screenshots land in test-results/misuse/.

CLEANUP IS VERIFIED, NOT ASSUMED. afterAll deletes every row this file creates, pass or fail. Post-run service-role check: customers named 'GARDEN BARN INC' back to 1; zero customers carrying this file's notes tag; zero evoucher_line_items against BRK-2026-0041; zero vouchers naming FWD202608-062. Nothing pre-existing was written to — the only rows touched are ones this file created. Dev only (oqermaidggvanahumjmj); supabase-prod was never opened.

TWO NOTES ON METHOD, both of which nearly produced false results.
1. K3 in a new costume: scenario 4 originally used the BD officer, who could not surface the rejected quotation at all — which would have read as 'the guard held' when it was really 'she cannot see the row'. Re-cast to the Pricing manager (quotations dial = 'everything') so the pass means what it says.
2. My first 'the guard held' assertion was almost inverted by a regex: the status menu's single entry 'Disapproved / Cancelled' matched /approv/. Terminal-to-terminal is not a way back. The filter now excludes it explicitly, and the spec prints the whole menu so the next reader can judge rather than trust.

THE THROUGH-LINE. Three of the five findings are the same shape: a field whose NAME promises one thing and whose VALUE is quietly something else — project_number holding a booking number, a header booking link left empty while the line has one, a customer row that is the second copy of itself. None of them involve a user doing anything wrong. Two of the three are caused by a single mislabelled prop (ExpensesTab.tsx:129), which is the closest thing this pass found to a one-line fix for a 249-row condition.

findings.what: Three click events dispatched in a single tick each run handleSubmit to completion, producing three separate numbered, approvable e-vouchers. `busy = isSaving || isUploading` and isSaving is react-query's isPending, which only becomes true AFTER handleSubmit has awaited the attachment upload — so the button's disabled attribute is set at least two async hops after the click that should have set it. Nothing between the click and the INSERT is idempotent.

handledWell: Real-mouse triple-click on Submit (three down/up pairs, 40ms apart) creates exactly ONE voucher — the modal unmounts on the first success so clicks two and three land on nothing. Guarded by the close rather than by the button, but genuinely guarded. This is the case a real hand produces; only the same-tick variant breaks.

Amount field, "1,500.00" — the one everybody predicts will break. type="number" makes the browser discard the separator before React sees it, so parseFloat gets a clean string and 1500.00 lands. Not the classic comma bug.
Amount field, "N/A" — refused by the input type; the empty string falls through `parseFloat(...) || 0` to a clean zero.
Type 2500 into the amount, delete it, try to submit empty — Submit stays disabled. An empty amount is 0 and 0 fails isFormValid.
Negative amount "-500" — the character is accepted by the number input, but Submit stays disabled, so no negative expense line can reach the AP chain.
Submit on a completely empty form — button disabled, nothing reachable.

unmeasured: Enter in a form text field — NOT REPRODUCIBLE and therefore deliberately not asserted. notes:
HARNESS HONESTY, because two false findings nearly shipped and both are the K-class shape.

FALSE FINDING 1: the first run of probe 1 reported "5 vouchers from 3 clicks" — duplicate_money, critical. It was 4 fixture vouchers plus one real one. The readback window was created_by=OpsTL AND created_at >= RUN_START, and the fixture vouchers are ALSO created_by the Ops TL and ALSO inserted after RUN_START. Fixed by excluding the fixture ids explicitly; the honest result is that the real-mouse triple-click HOLDS and only the same-tick variant breaks. The dramatic version of this finding was wrong.

FALSE FINDING 2: probe 4 originally called `selectOption()` on `locator("select")` for the Transaction Type. That control is a CustomDropdown (portalled, position:fixed), not a native select — the call matched nothing, threw into a .catch(), and the probe reported "the lines survived the type switch" while measuring an interaction that never happened. Same shape as K1: an unanswerable probe reading as a clean pass. It now asserts the panel title changed to "Cash Advance Request" before believing anything about the lines.

FALSE FINDING 3 (smaller): probe 8's queue search used the MISUSE tag. The approvals search box says "by number or requestor" and means it — it does not match `purpose`. The click failed, was swallowed by a .catch(), and "Approve is not offered" was reported as a clean result. It now looks up the evoucher_number with service-role and asserts the panel is open and armed BEFORE disturbing the record.

Also confirmed live in passing: finding L1 is real. A voucher raised through the form lands with header booking_id = NULL even though its line carries the link — which is why the readback in this file cannot be keyed on booking_id at all.

Every probe types in the UI, saves, and reads the row back with service-role (the supabase-js service client, not the actor's own session). Nine tests, all green, three consecutive clean runs. Fixtures tagged E2E-MISUSE and swept in afterAll; verified zero residue afterwards (evouchers / lines / bookings / projects / orphan lines all 0). Dev only, ref oqermaidggvanahumjmj — prod never touched, no migrations, no policy edits.

The two assertions written as CURRENT TRUTH rather than desired truth (the adversary convention) are probe 1b (expects >1 voucher) and probe 6 (expects exactly 1 note to survive). When either is fixed the test goes RED — that is the signal to update the expectation and strike the finding, not to loosen it.

findings.what: The inquiry insert is awaited and its error is caught; the handoff ticket that follows is fire-and-forget (`createWorkflowTicket(...).catch(console.error)`). Made only the tickets endpoint fail: the quotation landed, the user was told "Inquiry created.", and the ticket that is the entire mechanism by which Pricing learns the job exists was never written. Nobody is told, nobody looks. This does not need a hostile network — a policy denial or an FK error does it too, and the same pattern (`void recordNotificationEvent(...)`) sits on the e-voucher and invoice paths.

handledWell: OFFLINE MID-SAVE IS CORRECT, which is the headline good news given the brief. The save errored loudly, the form stayed filled with every field intact, and the database had zero rows — during the outage and again after reconnecting. Nothing replayed, nothing queued, no phantom success message. The worst outcome in the brief (a success toast with no row) did not happen here.
A 500 ON THE WRITE IS ALSO CORRECT. "Error saving inquiry: internal server error", still on the form, name field intact, zero rows. The UI does not claim success it did not get.

DOUBLE-SUBMIT ON A SLOW LINK IS GUARDED. Delayed the insert 4s and clicked Submit again 1.2s in: exactly one quotation row. `isSavingRef` in handleSaveInquiry catches it. Worth noting the guard is invisible — the button stays enabled and the label never changes to a busy state — so the user has no reason not to click again; but the data is safe.

UNICODE FROM WORD SURVIVES BYTE-IDENTICAL. Curly quotes, en-dash, em-dash and ellipsis all came back exactly as pasted. The name is uppercased, but that is AutoCapsProvider — a deliberate org-wide setting (org_settings.auto_caps_enabled, default ON) that rewrites every input value via the native setter — not corruption. Checking the source before reporting it is what kept this out of the findings list.

1366x768 AND THAT SCREEN AT 200% ZOOM BOTH HOLD. The action bar is sticky at the top, so Submit sits at y=32 of 768 and y=106 of 384, in the viewport without scrolling, and elementFromPoint at its own centre returns the button itself — not the E7 shape where a bare DIV intercepts the click. Screenshots in docs/qa/misuse-shots/.
A LAPTOP SET AHEAD OF UTC (UTC+14) agreed with the stored date on this run — only the behind-UTC direction skews. Recorded because it is what makes the single-timezone version of this test worthless.
unmeasured: ONLY ONE FORM WAS DRIVEN. Every condition here was applied to the BD inquiry form. It was chosen because its save path is representative — one awaited insert whose error is caught and toasted, then un-awaited follow-up writes whose errors are not — but the e-voucher, invoice and collection forms were NOT put through offline / 500 / session-expiry / double-submit. The half-save finding in particular should be re-run against the e-voucher, where the un-awaited write is the approval routing.

SESSION EXPIRY WAS SIMULATED, NOT AGED. The sb-* keys were cleared and the write was refused with a synthetic 401 PGRST301. A genuinely expired JWT would also exercise supabase-js's refresh path, which this did not. The observed silence may be the app's or the client's.

THE FIRE-AND-FORGET NOTIFICATION WRITE was not intercepted separately from the ticket write, so it is unknown whether recordNotificationEvent fails the same silent way. It is the same shape in the same function.

BFCACHE PROPER WAS NEVER EXERCISED. The builder pushes no history entry, so Back left the module entirely rather than restoring a stale form. The nastier half of that scenario — a stale form restored and then saved over newer data — could not be reached from this form and remains untested.

TWO SESSIONS ON THE SAME EXISTING RECORD was not run. Both sessions created new inquiries; neither edited a shared row, so the lost-update-on-details-JSONB case (M3) was not re-confirmed from the UI side.
THROTTLING WAS PER-REQUEST ROUTE DELAY, not a bandwidth profile — enough to open a real double-click window, not enough to test render-blocking or partial-response behaviour.

CONCURRENT-AGENT INTERFERENCE. Another agent ran its own specs against the same dev database and dev server mid-pass. It created a second customer named "FREIGHT CARE LOGISTICS" with no contacts, which broke three of my scenarios until the picker was hardened, and its Playwright runs twice wiped test-results/ (screenshots now go to docs/qa/misuse-shots/). Timings and any load-sensitive result from this pass should be treated as noisy.
notes:
TWO HARNESS LIES WERE CAUGHT AND FIXED BEFORE THEY BECAME FINDINGS. Both are the K1/K3 pattern in new costumes and are documented in the spec so the next pass inherits them.

(1) THE FIRST RUN LOOKED UP THE ROW BY `quotation_name = what I typed`, found nothing, and reported the control save as data_loss. The insert had in fact returned 201 and the row was there — under a name AutoCapsProvider had uppercased. Matching on what you typed cannot distinguish "no row" from "row, wrong value", which is exactly the distinction this tier exists to make. Every lookup now keys on a bare-digit run stamp and compares the full value afterwards.

(2) EVERY SCENARIO IN THE SECOND RUN CAME BACK "(no toast)" — including the control save, which definitely toasts "Inquiry created.". Sonner dismisses at ~4s; I read at 10s. "No error was shown" was a property of my harness, not the product, and had I shipped it I would have reported the offline and 500 cases as silent failures when both are actually correct and loud. Toasts are now recorded as they appear by an in-page poller installed before the click.

THE SHAPE OF THE RESULT. The awaited write is honest everywhere I pushed it — offline, 500, and (data-wise) session expiry all end with no row and no false success. What is not honest is everything the app does AFTER the awaited write: the handoff ticket, the notification. Those are un-awaited, their failures are swallowed, and the user is told the whole thing succeeded. That is the one finding here that is genuinely dangerous, and it is a pattern, not an instance.

The rest is the cost of a form that holds all its state in memory: refresh, Back, or a second person on the same login, and there is no draft, no warning and no conflict detection anywhere.
